title: Something Very Bad Is Gonna Happen
sourceTitle: Something Very Bad Is Gonna Happen
synopsis: You woke up at 4:11 a.m. with the deep, unshakable certainty that something very bad is about to happen — today, here, to someone you love. You have until the end of the day to figure out what, and whether you can stop it.

nodes.text: The feeling arrives before you're fully awake — heavy and certain, like furniture in a dark room. Something very bad is going to happen. You don't know what, only that it's today.

choices.text: Get up and write down everything you sense
choices.consequence: List the dread before it scatters.

choices.text: Try to go back to sleep — it's just a dream
choices.consequence: Denial is a curtain, not a door.

nodes.text: On a notepad you write: kitchen, car, your sister, the stairs at work, the bridge. Even reading it back, your hand shakes. Some of these mean nothing. One of them is the thing.

choices.text: Take the list seriously, item by item
choices.consequence: Superstition is sometimes pattern recognition.

choices.text: Burn the list and shake it off
choices.consequence: Naming a fear gives it shape.

nodes.text: By 7 a.m. you are pretending it's a normal day, with normal coffee. Your partner asks why you keep glancing at the door. You don't have a good answer. The feeling, in daylight, has not gotten smaller.

choices.text: Tell your partner the truth
choices.consequence: Saying it aloud is a kind of test.

choices.text: Keep it to yourself — they'll think you're spiraling
choices.consequence: Some weights are quieter alone.

nodes.text: She calls at 7:42 about nothing — running late, the car making a sound, did you call Mom. You hear, very clearly, the thing on your list. The car. The sound. Today.

choices.text: Tell her not to drive, no matter what
choices.consequence: Sometimes love sounds like a command.

choices.text: Ask careful questions without alarming her
choices.consequence: A net cast wider may catch more.

nodes.text: At work the stairwell looks longer than usual. The fluorescents tick. Your boss tells a story about a near-miss on the way in and you actually flinch — and notice that nobody else does.

choices.text: Take the stairs anyway
choices.consequence: Confront what your gut accuses.

choices.text: Take the elevator and feel ridiculous
choices.consequence: Some battles are not today's.

nodes.text: Your sister laughs — kindly. 'You're being weird,' she says. 'I love you. Bye.' She hangs up and you stand in your kitchen with the phone still warm, and the feeling thickens like fog.

choices.text: Drive to her right now
choices.consequence: Your body knows what your reasons don't.

choices.text: Trust her and turn your attention elsewhere
choices.consequence: You can't be in every room.

nodes.text: On the second floor you notice things — a damp patch on the ceiling near the server room, a colleague rubbing her chest, your phone buzzing with an unknown caller. The feeling is sharpening into specifics, but slowly, and not in time.

choices.text: Pull the fire alarm to clear the building
choices.consequence: Disruption now beats catastrophe later.

choices.text: Quietly tell your supervisor what you sense
choices.consequence: Authority lends courage to weird truths.

nodes.text: You're in your car heading to your sister's office or your own, depending — and you realize you're going too fast, and your hands are very cold. The feeling now includes you. Maybe the thing is you.

choices.text: Pull over and breathe before continuing
choices.consequence: You can't save anyone from a wreck you caused.

choices.text: Keep going — the urgency is the message
choices.consequence: Hesitation has a body count too.

nodes.text: Your supervisor frowns and humors you — but she also calls maintenance and tells the floor to stay clear of the stairwell. Small actions ripple. Maybe that's all it takes.

choices.text: Trust that small actions are enough
choices.consequence: Big disasters often arrive on small hinges.

choices.text: Push for a bigger response anyway
choices.consequence: Better foolish and safe than reasonable and sorry.

nodes.text: There is a sound — not big, not yet — somewhere across the city. A pop. A drop in air pressure. A siren two blocks over. The feeling now is a needle in your chest.

choices.text: Run toward the sound to help
choices.consequence: Compassion outruns dread, when it can.

choices.text: Find your people first
choices.consequence: You can't save the world without your own.

nodes.text: Mom: 'I had the strangest dream about you.' She is not psychic. She is, today, exactly as scared as you are. Until this moment you were maybe two thirds sure you weren't losing your mind.

choices.text: Tell her everything you've sensed
choices.consequence: Two witnesses make a fact.

choices.text: Lie to keep her calm
choices.consequence: Love and lying share a border.

nodes.text: Someone you love is here — your sister, your colleague, a stranger you couldn't reach — and the corridor smells like coffee and fear. The feeling has narrowed to one door and one held breath.

choices.text: Sit and wait for news
choices.consequence: Some battles are about endurance.

choices.text: Demand information from someone in scrubs
choices.consequence: Polite has a cost; impolite has a different one.

nodes.text: Your phone fills with alerts and your office goes on lockdown for a reason nobody upstairs has named yet. People text 'are you ok' and you can only answer 'I think so.' The feeling shrinks slightly — and gets darker.

choices.text: Help organize the people around you
choices.consequence: Action is the antidote to dread.

choices.text: Call everyone you love, in order
choices.consequence: Make sure they hear your voice today.

nodes.text: A nurse, a stranger, a child holds your hand for a moment. Whatever the catastrophe was or wasn't, the day is still full of small good people. The feeling does not lift. It just becomes survivable.

choices.text: Notice the goodness and let it steady you
choices.consequence: Beauty doesn't cancel dread; it carries it.

choices.text: Keep scanning for the next danger
choices.consequence: Vigilance is hard to switch off.

nodes.text: The first reports are wrong, like they always are. Then the second reports are wrong differently. Eventually a true sentence arrives, and it is both better and worse than what your body told you at 4:11.

choices.text: Sit with the true sentence
choices.consequence: Truth is a posture you have to settle into.

choices.text: Try to make sense of why you felt it
choices.consequence: Meaning is a balm and sometimes a trap.

nodes.text: The day is winding down without ending you. Your sister is alive, or recovering, or grieving someone else; either way, she is on the other end of a phone call, breathing. You sit by a window and watch the city's lights come on.

choices.text: Decide the feeling was real and useful
choices.consequence: Believe your body next time, too.

choices.text: Decide it was coincidence with bad timing
choices.consequence: Skepticism is a kind of mercy on yourself.

nodes.text: A second wave hits — a smaller thing, a near-miss, a phone call about a different cousin. The feeling is now a familiar weight, no longer a stranger. You will, you realize, live the rest of your life with this voice.

choices.text: Make peace with the voice and listen carefully
choices.consequence: A reliable warning is a strange gift.

choices.text: Decide to fight the voice with therapy and routine
choices.consequence: You don't have to inherit your own dread forever.

nodes.text: An ordinary hour again. You light a candle for no reason and notice you didn't get killed today, and neither did the people you love most. That is not a small thing. That is, in fact, the only thing.

choices.text: Call your mother before bed
choices.consequence: The bad things will or won't come. Love now.

choices.text: Write down what you learned today
choices.consequence: Memory is the only seatbelt against forgetting.

nodes.text: You won't tell most people about this day. You'll carry it like a small smooth stone in a pocket — a reminder that catastrophe was once close, and the city kept going, and so did you. It is, somehow, comforting.

choices.text: Keep the stone and the lesson
choices.consequence: Some weights are also anchors.

choices.text: Put the stone down and walk lighter
choices.consequence: You're allowed to forget on purpose.

nodes.text: You call them — sister, partner, mother, the friend you've been meaning to. Not big speeches. Just 'I love you, I'm glad you're here.' Some of them cry a little. Most of them say 'are you okay?' You are. You are.

choices.text: Make this your new ordinary
choices.consequence: Call the people now, before the next 4:11.

choices.text: Drift back to your old habits in a week
choices.consequence: Even good lessons need re-learning.

nodes.text: Sleep doesn't come fast. The feeling, just before you drift off, returns gently — but this time it's not a warning. It's the simple bedrock fact that you are mortal, and so is everyone you love, and tonight, again, nobody is gone.

choices.text: Sleep with the knowledge as a comfort
choices.consequence: Mortality is also permission to love now.

choices.text: Sleep with one eye open from now on
choices.consequence: Vigilance can be a vow, not a curse.

nodes.text: You don't get more days than you got. You get to do something with the ones you have. The feeling becomes a quiet companion — not a fortune teller, not a curse — just the part of you that has noticed how lucky you are, and how briefly.
Time blunts the day. You forget some of the details and remember the rest wrong. That is okay. Most of being human is forgetting what almost killed you and showing up to dinner anyway.

You become someone who picks up the phone fast, who locks the door, who checks the smoke detector twice. People tease you for it. People also, on the worst day of their lives, call you first. You are, in a way nobody planned, useful.
